about.title: Lake Forest Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lake Forest is a city of roughly 82,000 people, and most of its daily errands happen on private property: grocery aisles, restaurant patios, office lobbies, apartment stairwells, and the parking lots that line El Toro Road, Lake Forest Drive, and Bake Parkway. When a floor is left slick or a curb goes unrepaired, the person who falls is often told it was their own clumsiness. California law sees it differently. A property owner or business in Lake Forest generally has a duty to fix hazards it knew about, or reasonably should have discovered, and to warn visitors in the meantime. Proving that notice is the heart of the claim, which is why photographs, incident reports, and store surveillance footage matter so much in the first days. Under Orange County's civil rules you generally have two years to file, and that window narrows sharply if the property belongs to a city, school district, or other public entity. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, for free, with an independent attorney who reviews your fall and explains your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Lake Forest Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Hard Part, and Timing Helps
items.desc: California asks whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know to request cleaning logs, inspection schedules, and video before it is overwritten, which is often within days.

items.title: Two Years Is Not Always Two Years
items.desc: A fall at a private store in Lake Forest generally carries a two-year filing deadline, but a fall on public property involves a much shorter government claim requirement. An independent attorney can sort out which clock applies to you.

items.title: Partial Blame Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were looking at your phone or wearing sandals, you may still recover a reduced share. No one in our network charges a fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I fell in a shopping center parking lot off El Toro Road. Who is actually responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who controlled the area where you fell. A shopping center owner, a property management company, and an individual tenant may each hold some responsibility for parking lots and walkways in Lake Forest. An attorney can review lease terms and maintenance agreements to identify the right parties, which is not something the injured person is expected to figure out alone.

items.question: What should I document right after a slip and fall?
items.answer: Photograph the exact spot, the hazard itself, your footwear, and any missing warning signs before conditions change. Ask for an incident report and the names of employees or witnesses, and request in writing that surveillance video be preserved. Seek medical care the same day, since a gap in treatment is often used to question the injury later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with a Lake Forest attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service and not a law firm; we connect you with an independent attorney who handles premises liability cases in Orange County. That attorney works on contingency, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery. The initial review of your situation costs nothing.
